title: The database AI agents build on just raised $150M.
caption:
Two founders built the database AI agents now build on. They just raised $150M.

Supabase sets up an app's back end (data, logins, files) in a few clicks. Paul Copplestone, a New Zealander, met Ant Wilson at Entrepreneur First in Singapore; they started it in 2020. Paul told Fortune an earlier startup ran out of money, and that the name is partly a Nicki Minaj joke.

The twist: someone else launched it. Paul says it was posted on Hacker News the day after he called it an "open source Firebase alternative," and it shot to the top.

Now Supabase says it adds 4 million databases a month, 70% created by AI agents or AI tools. On Oct 2, Singapore's GIC led a $150M round with Alphabet's CapitalG. Y Combinator says it values Supabase at $10.65B, barely above June's $10.5B.

Our take: name the giant you replace, then outgrow it.

Would you trust a database a robot made?

In June, Supabase's CEO said Anthropic's Claude Code was the "largest contributor" to its growth since the start of the year.
